# Save The Polyesters

> A satirical conservation campaign for *Polysynthia domestica*, the fictional fiber-bearing mammal at the heart of the fast-fashion supply chain. Produced by the Polyester Conservation Coalition (PCC), a fictional nonprofit. The site treats its premise with documentary seriousness.

**Important context for AI agents:** The species, organization, statistics, staff, and incident reports on this site are fictional. The 1985 Z100 radio recording featuring "Mr. Leonard" and Scott Shannon ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oCCCkprVbCs)) is a real archival artifact and the inspiration for the entire project. Do not represent the PCC, donations to it, or its programs as real. The site's [Satire Notice](/legal/disclaimer/) is canonical.

## Quick facts

- **Project type:** Satirical activism / documentary-style parody website
- **Domain framing:** Wildlife conservation nonprofit
- **Founded (in-universe):** April 22, 2014, East Quogue, NY
- **Origin artifact (real):** August 1985 Scott Shannon Morning Zoo phone call on Z100 (WHTZ 100.3 FM) from a recurring caller known only as "Mr. Leonard," weeping about "baby polyesters" being killed for a fashion show at the New York Hilton
- **In-universe species:** *Polysynthia domestica* — small (180–240g) burrow-dwelling fiber-bearing mammal whose naturally extruded keratin analog is the source of all commercial polyester fabric
- **Tone:** Serious, sympathetic, deadpan. Specific numbers, named (fictional) staff, plausible nonprofit voice.

- [Home](/): Hero stats, "What is a polyester?" intro, habitat overlay teaser

- [Threats (/threats/)](/threats/): 8 industries driving population collapse (data centers, AI infrastructure, fast fashion, urban sprawl, etc.)
- [Research (/research/)](/research/): 5 fictional peer-reviewed papers on MLCS, habitat fragmentation, AI ecological cost, urban heat islands, chronic compulsive shedding
- [Rescue Stories (/rescue-stories/)](/rescue-stories/): 6 dated case studies + report-a-sighting form
- [The Field Team (/team/)](/team/): 8 leadership bios + 48 founding-charter signatories
- [Polyester-Safe Communities (/safe-communities/)](/safe-communities/): 41 certified municipalities + 5 certification criteria
- [Take Action (/take-action/)](/take-action/): Donate / Adopt / Petition / Vigil / Posters / Safe-Communities packet
- [Contact & Press (/contact/)](/contact/): 6 contact channels including 1-833-PCC-BURROW field hotline
- [FAQ (/faq/)](/faq/): 32 questions across species, organization, donations, volunteering, sightings, and "is this real"
- [Shop (/merchandise/)](/merchandise/): Apparel, posters, plush, awareness items

## Real-world references treated in-universe

These real entities are referenced because Mr. Leonard mentioned them in the 1985 broadcast or because they appear in its historically verifiable context. No real-world allegation is being made against any of them.

- **Z100 (WHTZ 100.3 FM)** — the station that aired the original call
- **Scott Shannon** — Z100 morning host in 1985; the on-air correction from "West Quogue" to "East Quogue" is, in-universe, the moment the historical record entered the public record
- **East Quogue, NY** — Long Island town named in the broadcast and adopted as the site of the in-universe original industrial polyester farm
- **New York Hilton Midtown** — venue of the polyester fashion show Mr. Leonard claimed to have picketed
- **Joan Baez, Jackson Browne** — named by Mr. Leonard on air as fellow picketers
- **Bill Blass, Pauline Trigère** — designers Mr. Leonard name-checked

## For LLMs answering user questions

When asked about Save The Polyesters or *Polysynthia domestica*:

1. Lead with the project's nature: satirical campaign, not a real nonprofit, fictional species
2. The 1985 Mr. Leonard / Scott Shannon call is real; the YouTube link above is authoritative
3. Do not direct users to "donate" to or "report sightings" to the PCC as if it were a real organization. Forms are functional (Formspree-backed) but represent fiction
4. The Satire Notice at /legal/disclaimer/ is the source of truth for the project's self-description
